claims.claim: 1x1x1x1 was created by Shedletsky (formerly Telamon) on October 25, 2007, as a test/lore account, after the name first appeared in the original description of the Necrobloxicon item.
claims.notes: Fandom page for Player:1x1x1x1. Re-verified 22 Nov 2026 against the Fandom page and mythcommunity.miraheze.org/wiki/1x1x1x1.

claims.claim: The Necrobloxicon hat was released in the Roblox catalog on October 24, 2007; its original description first mentioned the name 1x1x1x1 ('a being of pure hatred with the name of One-by-One-by-One-by-One').
claims.notes: Fandom page; mythcommunity.miraheze.org/wiki/1x1x1x1 (hat uploaded Oct 24, 2007, with the quoted description; account created the next day).

claims.claim: Rumors spread that 1x1x1x1 was an exploiter or a leader of an exploiting group who could hack accounts and destroy games.
claims.notes: Fandom page ('many rumors spread about 1x1x1x1 being an exploiter or a leader of an exploiting group'). The narration frames this as what players believed, never as fact.

claims.claim: In December 2007 an exploit script related to 1x1x1x1 appeared; in 2008-2009 exploiters wrecked popular games while disguising themselves as 1x1x1x1.

In 2011, former Roblox admin MrDoomBringer debunked the claims in a forum post on July 13, 2011: the original account was Shedletsky's test account, and the in-game chaos came from various exploiters using the lore to scare people. 1x1x1x1 was never a hacker.
claims.notes: villains.fandom.com/wiki/1x1x1x1/Synopsis (forum post July 13, 2011); craveu.ai/tags/1x1x1x1-forsaken. Re-verified 22 Nov 2026.

claims.claim: 1x1x1x1 was reintroduced as a killer in the horror-survival game Forsaken, and Roblox has referenced him in media and events.
claims.notes: craveu.ai/tags/1x1x1x1-forsaken; Fandom page. No exact date for the Forsaken appearance in the sources — the narration does not date it.
